On the left side there is a dark vertical rectangle, extending from the top of the flag all the way to the bottom. The right side is horizontally divided into two rectangles, upper and lower: the upper one is a gray rectangle, and the lower one is a white rectangle; these two rectangles on the right side appear to have the same width and the same height. Reasoning: Let the height of the white rectangle be h and the width be w. The gray rectangle is directly above the white rectangle and has the same dimensions as the white rectangle, so the total height on the right side is 2h. The dark rectangle on the left side also exactly occupies the entire height of the flag, so its height is also 2h. The problem says the flag is divided into three equal rectangles, so the dark rectangle on the left side is congruent to the white rectangle, only rotated in direction; therefore the vertical side of the dark rectangle on the left side is equal to the width w of the white rectangle. Thus w = 2h, so the side-length ratio of the white rectangle is h:w = 1:2.

method.method_draft: View the diagram as a tiling by three identical copies of one rectangle. The white rectangle is one copy. The dark rectangle on the left is another copy rotated 90 degrees, because it has the same size as the white rectangle but is placed vertically. In the picture, the height of this rotated dark copy is exactly the combined height of the gray and white rectangles on the right.
